_readme: The ledger. One record per (subject, axis) pair -- every pair, always: an absent cell is a
DEFECT, not a zero, because 'nobody looked' and 'we looked and found nothing' are different
claims and mp_metric.validate() refuses to score a census that writes them identically.
It is EMPTY on purpose. Every non-zero cell must carry a retrievable artifact -- url,
retrieval date, and the sha256 of the bytes actually retrieved. Seeding this file with
plausible-looking scores would be the precise defect this instrument exists to detect, so
the first subject is added only when its artifacts have been fetched and hashed by
fetch_artifact.py.
subject record:  {"id": "llama-3.1-8B", "kind": "open-weights", "note": "..."}
kind is one of: fully-open | open-weights | api-only | historical-control
cell record:
"subject":  "llama-3.1-8B",
"axis":     2,
"score":    2,                 2 CHECKED | 1 CLAIMED | 0 ABSENT | null N/A
"check":    "scripts/check_corpus_digest.py -- recomputed and compared",
"na_reason": "only when score is null; bulk N/A is the escape hatch",
"note":     "free text for a human reader"
A score of 2 additionally requires `check`: the scripted check that was actually run.
Without it the cell is a 1 -- somebody's reading of a document -- not a 2.
as_of is the census date. Releases change: a model card edited after scoring silently
invalidates a cell, so every evidence record is re-fetched and re-hashed before submission
and any digest that moved is a finding, not a maintenance chore.
selection_rule: SELECTION-RULE.md, committed and OpenTimestamped before any cell existed

subjects.note: the census's positive control: if the release that publishes the most cannot score well, the instrument is wrong
second fully-open reference point; the stratum is taken whole

open-weights stratum, selected by download rank
